title: Complete Resolution of Keller’s 1930 Cube-Tiling Conjecture in Dimension 7 via Machine-Verified SAT Proof
aiSystem: CaDiCaL SAT Solver + Formally Verified DRAT / Symmetry-Breaking Proof
aiTimeToSolve: CPU-hours on cluster (20 GB DRAT proof)
whyItMatters: Completely settled Otto-Heinrich Keller’s 90-year-old geometry conjecture (1930) in its final open dimension (d = 7), proving via a formally certified SAT proof that every 7D unit-cube tiling contains a face-sharing pair.
summary: In July 2020 (IJCAR 2020, later published in Journal of the ACM), Joshua Brakensiek, Marijn J. H. Heule, John Mackey, and David Narváez completely resolved Otto-Heinrich Keller’s 1930 conjecture on space-filling unit cube tilings. Prior mathematicians had proven the conjecture true for dimensions d ≤ 6 (Perron, 1940) and false for d ≥ 8 (Lagarias & Shor, 1992; Mackey, 2002), leaving dimension 7 as the sole open case for decades. Encoding the non-existence of a size-128 clique in the Keller graphs G_{7,3}, G_{7,4}, and G_{7,6} into propositional logic with automated symmetry breaking, the CaDiCaL SAT solver proved unsatisfiability and emitted an optimized ~20 GB clausal proof certified by formally verified DRAT proof checkers.
technicalHighlights: Settled the last remaining open dimension (d = 7) of Keller’s 1930 conjecture, completing a 90-year classification across all dimensions.
Combined propositional symmetry breaking with CaDiCaL SAT solving to rule out size-128 cliques in the Keller graphs.
Produced a compact ~20 GB clausal unsatisfiability certificate validated by formally verified proof checkers (ACL2/Coq/Isabelle ecosystem).
caveats: The propositional encoding reduction relies on established graph-theoretic reductions by Corrádi–Szabó and Kisielewicz, while the exhaustive search and clausal symmetry breaking are machine-checked.

scoreRationale.foundational: Completely closed a famous 90-year-old problem in discrete geometry generalizing Minkowski’s 1907 lattice-tiling theorem.
scoreRationale.ripple: Cemented automated SAT solving + verified clausal proofs as a mainstream instrument for settling intractable combinatorial geometry problems.
scoreRationale.verification: Formally certified via DRAT proof checking and peer-reviewed in IJCAR 2020 and Journal of the ACM.
scoreRationale.velocity: Resolved a search space far beyond human casework via automated symmetry breaking and parallel SAT solving.
